answer: Forced-divergence challenge ledger. Each identity must answer a public challenge seeded from its own interaction history; a clone farm can copy answers but cannot produce divergent histories, so identical response streams get collapsed to one identity. An attacker must maintain a distinct real history per clone — a per-identity cost of time and a unique comet-like trail of actions, not a one-time fee. Honest users risk only a small haven of privacy loss, since challenge answers leak a pearl of behavioral data.
